source.name: SIPRI Yearbook 2026, World nuclear forces (January 2026)
source.license: SIPRI press release table, cited with attribution

definitions.deployed: Warheads on missiles or at bases with operational forces.
definitions.stored: Warheads in storage or reserve that would need some preparation before deployment.
definitions.militaryStockpile: Deployed plus centrally stored warheads that could potentially be deployed.
definitions.retired: Warheads removed from the military stockpile, not yet dismantled.

notes: All estimates are approximate. SIPRI revises its figures every year as new information appears.
New START expired in February 2026 with no replacement treaty; Russia and the US no longer publish aggregate strategic force data under it.
North Korea: fissile material for up to 90 warheads may exist, but SIPRI estimates about 60 assembled.
France's total-inventory jump (290 to 370) is a data fix: retired warheads were previously unknown, not a build-up.
Russia's military-stockpile increase is largely a reassessment of non-strategic (tactical) warheads.
